In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}}}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).$
